title: The life of Jesus
intro: The main events of Jesus’ life on earth in time order. Zoom in on 33 C.E. to follow his last week day by day.

items.name: Birth and early life
items.text: From the announcements of John’s and Jesus’ births to the start of John the Baptist’s ministry. Jesus grows up in Nazareth, subject to his parents, and learns carpentry.

pictures.title: Angels Announce the Birth of Jesus

items.name: Beginning of his ministry
items.text: From his baptism to his leaving Judea for Galilee after John is imprisoned.

items.name: Great ministry in Galilee
items.text: Jesus makes Capernaum his base, chooses the twelve, gives the Sermon on the Mount and makes three preaching tours of Galilee.

items.name: Later ministry in Judea and Perea
items.text: From the Festival of Tabernacles in Jerusalem, through his teaching east of the Jordan, to his arrival near Jerusalem for the last Passover.

items.name: Final days in Jerusalem
items.text: The last week before his death, his resurrection on Nisan 16, and the forty days until he ascends to heaven.

items.name: Gabriel foretells John’s birth
items.text: At the temple in Jerusalem the angel Gabriel tells the priest Zechariah that his wife Elizabeth will have a son, John.

items.name: Gabriel visits Mary
items.text: In Nazareth, Gabriel tells Mary she will give birth to Jesus. She visits her relative Elizabeth in Judea.

items.name: Jesus is born in Bethlehem
items.text: Jesus is born. An angel announces the good news to shepherds, who visit the infant. He is circumcised on the eighth day and later presented at the temple.

pictures.title: Angels Announce the Birth of Jesus

items.name: Astrologers visit; flight to Egypt
items.text: Astrologers visit. The family flees to Egypt, Herod has the young boys killed, and after returning the family settles in Nazareth.

items.name: Twelve-year-old Jesus at the temple
items.text: Jesus questions the teachers at the temple, then returns to Nazareth and continues subject to his parents.

items.name: John the Baptist begins his ministry
items.text: In the wilderness by the Jordan River, John begins preaching and baptizing.

items.name: Jesus is baptized and anointed
items.text: At the Jordan River Jesus is baptized and anointed. Jehovah declares him his Son and approves him.

items.name: Tempted by the Devil
items.text: In the Judean wilderness Jesus is tempted by the Devil and rejects each temptation.

items.name: First disciples; first miracle
items.text: John identifies Jesus as the Lamb of God and the first disciples join him. At a wedding in Cana he turns water into wine.

items.name: Cleanses the temple; talks with Nicodemus
items.text: In Jerusalem Jesus drives the sellers out of the temple and explains to Nicodemus what it means to be born again.

items.name: John imprisoned; teaches the Samaritans
items.text: John is put in prison and Jesus leaves for Galilee. On the way he teaches a Samaritan woman at a well near Sychar.

items.name: Announces: “The Kingdom has drawn near”
items.text: Jesus begins his great ministry in Galilee. He reads from the scroll of Isaiah at Nazareth and moves to Capernaum.

items.name: Calls four fishermen
items.text: By the Sea of Galilee he calls Simon and Andrew, James and John, and makes his first tour of Galilee with them.

items.name: Heals a paralytic; calls Matthew
items.text: At Capernaum he heals a paralyzed man, then calls Matthew and dines with tax collectors.

items.name: Heals a sick man at Bethzatha
items.text: In Jerusalem he heals a man on the Sabbath, and the Jews seek to kill him.

items.name: Chooses the 12 apostles
items.text: On a mountain near Capernaum, after praying all night, he chooses twelve apostles.

items.name: Sermon on the Mount
items.text: Near Capernaum he gives the Sermon on the Mount.

items.name: Resurrects a widow’s son
items.text: At Nain he raises a widow’s only son. He then makes a second preaching tour of Galilee with the twelve.

items.name: Kingdom illustrations; calms a storm
items.text: He teaches the crowds with illustrations about the Kingdom and calms a storm on the Sea of Galilee.

items.name: Raises Jairus’ daughter
items.text: He heals a woman with a flow of blood and brings the daughter of Jairus back to life.

items.name: Sends out the apostles; John is beheaded
items.text: On a third tour of Galilee he sends the apostles out to preach. Herod has John the Baptist beheaded.

items.name: Feeds 5,000; walks on the sea
items.text: He feeds about 5,000 men. The crowd tries to make him king. He walks on the sea and later calls himself the bread of life, and many leave him.

items.name: Foretells his death; the transfiguration
items.text: Near Caesarea Philippi he speaks of the keys of the Kingdom and foretells his death and resurrection. On a mountain, probably Hermon, he is transfigured and Jehovah speaks.

items.name: Teaches at the Festival of Tabernacles
items.text: In Jerusalem he teaches at the festival, says “I am the light of the world,” and heals a man born blind.

items.name: Sends out the 70
items.when: 32 C.E., after the Festival of Tabernacles
items.text: He sends out seventy disciples, gives the illustration of the neighborly Samaritan and visits the home of Martha and Mary.

items.name: “The fine shepherd”
items.text: In Jerusalem he gives the illustration of the fine shepherd. The Jews try to stone him and he leaves for Bethany across the Jordan.

items.name: Teaches in Perea
items.text: Traveling toward Jerusalem he teaches in the cities and villages of Perea, giving the illustrations of the lost sheep, the lost coin and the lost son.

items.name: Resurrects Lazarus
items.text: At Bethany, Lazarus dies and Jesus brings him back to life. The leaders plot to kill Jesus.

items.name: Heals blind men; visits Zacchaeus
items.text: Passing through Jericho on the way to Jerusalem he heals two blind men and visits Zacchaeus.

items.name: Arrives at Bethany
items.text: Jesus arrives six days before the Passover.

items.name: Enters Jerusalem on a donkey
items.text: Mary pours oil on his head and feet at Bethany. He then enters Jerusalem triumphantly, riding on a donkey.

items.name: Cleanses the temple again
items.text: He curses a fig tree and cleanses the temple a second time. The chief priests scheme to destroy him. Jehovah speaks from heaven.

items.name: Teaches in the temple; the sign of his presence
items.text: His authority is challenged. He answers questions on Caesar, the resurrection and the greatest commandment, pronounces woes on the scribes and Pharisees, and on the Mount of Olives gives the sign of his future presence.

items.name: Leaders plot; Judas arranges the betrayal
items.text: The Jewish leaders plot to kill him and Judas arranges to betray him.

items.name: Prepares for the last Passover
items.text: Jesus sends disciples to prepare the Passover.

items.name: Passover; the Lord’s Evening Meal
items.text: He eats the Passover with the apostles, washes their feet, dismisses Judas and institutes the Lord’s Evening Meal. He gives the command to love and prays with them.

items.name: Gethsemane: betrayal and arrest
items.text: After his agony in the garden he is betrayed and arrested.

items.name: Trials; Peter denies him
items.text: He is questioned by Annas, tried by Caiaphas and the Sanhedrin, and Peter denies him. He is taken to Pilate, to Herod and back to Pilate, who sentences him to death.

items.name: Dies at Golgotha
items.text: Jesus dies on the torture stake. His body is taken down and placed in a tomb.

items.name: Tomb sealed and guarded
items.text: The priests and Pharisees get a guard for the tomb and seal it.

items.name: Jesus is resurrected
items.text: Jesus is resurrected and appears five times to disciples that day.

items.name: More appearances; the commission
items.text: In Jerusalem and Galilee he appears to the disciples again, instructs them and commissions them to make disciples.

items.name: Ascends to heaven
items.text: From the Mount of Olives, on the fortieth day after his resurrection, Jesus ascends to heaven.
